az_library_the.blurb: A short sandstone cliff above the East Verde River, roughly two miles north of Payson off the highway. Two prominent dihedrals in the middle give it its name. Lines run about 40 to 60 feet and split fairly evenly between gear routes and bolted ones, with a few top-rope options. Most of the grades sit in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a handful of 5.12s above and a few moderates from 5.6 to 5.9 below. The wall is clean and straightforward, though some climbers find the ratings stiff. Most of the lines are toward the right side of the wall. Expect a quick but loose scramble to the base.
az_library_the.parking_note: Pull off on the east side of the highway just south of the East Verde bridge, about two miles north of Payson; the walk to the cliff starts from there.

az_south_fin.blurb: A granite fin at Windy Point, high on the Catalina Highway above Tucson on Mount Lemmon. The overlook lot is only a few minutes from the cliff, and routes face both sides of the fin, so you can pick sun or shade. The rock is considered very good and the fin holds many two- and three-star lines. Bolted and gear routes are about evenly split. Grades run mostly from 5.9 to 5.12, with a few easy gear climbs below that, and the 5.11s and 5.12s make up roughly half the list. Windy Point sits at mid-elevation, so it stays comfortable well beyond the hot months.

az_rough_rider_wall.blurb: A steep, orange wall in the Homestead zone of central Arizona, more than 100 feet tall and facing west, so it gets morning shade. All routes are bolted and long, often finishing under roofs, with positive holds and buckets on clean lines. Bring a 70 m rope, plenty of quickdraws and stamina. Grades are hard: nearly everything falls between 5.11 and 5.12, with only a couple of 5.10s, making it a spot for strong sport climbers. Most climbers skip it in the coldest months.

az_joint_the.blurb: A small granite crag in Stewart Pocket, a few miles southeast of Payson. Its east-facing wall catches morning sun and goes shady after noon. Routes are short, mostly 40 to 50 feet, and offer a mix of bolted lines, gear climbs and top-ropes, plus a single aid route. Grades cover a wide range, from 5.3 up to a 5.12 project, with the bulk between 5.6 and 5.10 and a few 5.11s. Every route has anchors on top, and you can walk off the west side, so most lines can be top-roped with some effort. Follow the Boulders North trail and turn off where a small pile of stones and logs marks the side path.

az_throne_universe_wall_the.blurb: A wall in Upper Devils Canyon, part of the Queen Creek Canyon climbing zone near Oak Flat Campground in central Arizona. The canyon runs north to south and its walls mostly face east, so routes are best after mid-morning on cooler summer days. Most of the 24 climbs here are bolted, with a few gear lines. Grades span the 5.6 to 5.10 range, led by 5.7s, and tail off into a few 5.11s and a single 5.12. Pockets and edges both show up on the holds.

az_sheepshead_the.blurb: A big granite dome in the western Dragoon Mountains of southern Arizona, within the West Cochise Stronghold. Expect committing, multi-pitch routes, some of them runout, on polished slabs and plates with chicken-head holds. The list here is mostly gear routes with a good share of bolted lines and two aid climbs, and almost everything sits at 5.10, with a few easier and a few 5.11s. Take time on the approach: a cairned use trail crosses a grassy field and drainages to the base, and it can overgrow after the monsoon. Granite becomes slippery when wet. A dirt road leads to the parking area.

az_nursery_the.blurb: A beginner-friendly section of Lower Sullivan Canyon near Prescott, known for short cracks. The rock is pocketed basalt, which takes nuts and cams well, though some cams can feel fiddly. Nearly everything is traditional protection, with one short bolt-protected line and a single top-rope option; local climbers generally dislike new bolting. Grades start at 5.5 and run to 5.10, with most lines in the 5.8 to 5.9 band. Anchors are usually bolted, but the clifftop is strewn with loose blocks, so avoid walking up to set top-ropes from above. Reach the far east side by dropping down the concrete gully and heading west past the cave.
